previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including end-stage renal disease, recurrent Clostridium difficile infection, atrial fibrillation, and severe aortic stenosis was admitted for increased diarrhea over four days, concerning for relapse. She had recently completed a course of vancomycin for C. diff but reported recurrence of watery, green stools despite initial improvement. Stool testing was negative for toxigenic C. difficile and other pathogens. She remained afebrile without dehydration and had only one loose stool during admission. Given her high risk for recurrence, the decision was made to extend oral vancomycin with a taper. Her warfarin was adjusted due to a supratherapeutic INR of 2.9, and she restarted dialysis without complications. She was discharged home after clinical improvement with plans to taper omeprazole, follow up with cardiology for aortic stenosis, and continue outpatient management of hyperparathyroidism and hypercalcemia.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile

cardiac border is difficult to assess due to the right-sided opacity.  The
left aspect of the cardiac and mediastinal silhouette is stable.  There is no

quadrant.

IMPRESSION:  Moderate right and small left pleural effusions, increased on the
right and stable to possibly slightly increased on the left.  Right base
opacity may be due to combination of pleural effusion and atelectasis, but
consolidation is not excluded.  Prominence of the hila possibly due to
vascular congestion is again seen.
